title: Indoor Coil Temperature Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Indoor coil thermistor open or short.
fullDescription: Goodman E1 on AC systems indicates the indoor coil temperature sensor is out of range. The system uses this sensor to prevent coil freeze-up.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power at the breaker before opening control panels. High-voltage capacitors can hold a lethal charge even after power is removed.

fixSteps.title: Re-seat Connector
fixSteps.instruction: Open the air handler and verify the coil sensor plug is fully seated.

fixSteps.title: Test Resistance
fixSteps.instruction: Compare thermistor resistance to spec chart at room temperature.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Clip the new sensor to the coil at the same location.

whenToCallPro: If sensor and wiring check good, a pro should test the board.

faq.a: Frozen coils block airflow and can damage the compressor with liquid floodback.

title: Outdoor Ambient Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Outdoor temperature thermistor open or short.
fullDescription: Goodman E2 indicates the outdoor unit's ambient temperature sensor reading is out of valid range. Some staging logic depends on this sensor.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power at the breaker before opening control panels. High-voltage capacitors can hold a lethal charge even after power is removed.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check sensor wires for chafing, ant damage, or rodent chewing.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Measure resistance and compare to chart.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new thermistor in original location.

whenToCallPro: If sensor checks good, board may need testing.

faq.a: Mounted in the outdoor coil airflow path away from the compressor heat.

title: Discharge Pipe Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Compressor discharge thermistor out of range.
fullDescription: Goodman E3 means the discharge line temperature sensor on the outdoor unit is reading invalid values. This sensor protects the compressor from overheat.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Improper handling can cause frostbite, asphyxiation, or environmental harm.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Clamp
fixSteps.instruction: Verify thermistor is firmly attached to the discharge line.

fixSteps.title: Replace Thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new discharge sensor with thermal paste under clamp.

whenToCallPro: Pro recommended due to refrigerant proximity.

faq.q: Can I run AC with E3?
faq.a: Possible but unsafe - compressor may overheat without this protection.

title: High Pressure Protection
shortDescription: High side pressure exceeded safe threshold.
fullDescription: Goodman E4 indicates the high-pressure switch on the discharge line has tripped. The compressor stops to prevent damage.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Improper handling can cause frostbite, asphyxiation, or environmental harm.

fixSteps.title: Wash Coil
fixSteps.instruction: Rinse outdoor coil with garden hose from inside out.

fixSteps.title: Verify Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm fan runs continuously with compressor.

faq.a: At least once a year, more in dusty or pollen-heavy areas.

title: Low Pressure Protection
fullDescription: Goodman E5 indicates the low-pressure switch has opened, signaling refrigerant starvation in the system.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Improper handling can cause frostbite, asphyxiation, or environmental harm.
symptoms: Ice on indoor coil or suction line

fixSteps.title: Replace Filter
fixSteps.instruction: Restore airflow to allow coil to thaw.

fixSteps.title: Run Fan Only
fixSteps.instruction: Set thermostat to fan-only for 2 hours to defrost coil.

fixSteps.title: Pro Leak Check
fixSteps.instruction: Tech to perform leak detection and recharge.

whenToCallPro: Leak repairs and recharge are professional jobs.

faq.a: Low refrigerant or low airflow drops coil temperature below freezing.

title: Compressor Overload
fullDescription: Goodman E6 means the compressor's internal thermal overload has opened due to overheating or overcurrent.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Improper handling can cause frostbite, asphyxiation, or environmental harm.

fixSteps.title: Test Capacitor
fixSteps.instruction: Discharge and measure run cap microfarads.

fixSteps.title: Check Voltage
fixSteps.instruction: Measure 240V supply at disconnect under load.

whenToCallPro: Compressor diagnostics belong to a pro.

faq.q: Can a bad cap kill a compressor?
faq.a: Yes - prolonged operation with a weak run cap stresses the windings.

title: Communication Fault
shortDescription: Indoor and outdoor units lost communication.
fullDescription: Goodman E7 (ComfortNet systems) indicates a communication loss on the data bus between thermostat, indoor unit, and outdoor unit.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power at the breaker before opening control panels. High-voltage capacitors can hold a lethal charge even after power is removed.

causes.cause: Wrong wire colors at one end

symptoms: Thermostat blank or in non-comm mode

fixSteps.title: Re-seat Terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Tighten R, C, 1, 2 bus terminals at all three points.

fixSteps.title: Verify Polarity
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm matching colors on Data 1 and Data 2 terminals.

whenToCallPro: If wiring is good and fault persists, board diagnosis needed.

faq.a: Goodman's communicating system using a 4-wire bus for staging and diagnostics.

title: Outdoor Fan Motor Fault
fullDescription: Goodman E8 indicates the outdoor fan motor is not running when commanded. The compressor will be locked out to prevent high-pressure damage.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power at the breaker before opening control panels. High-voltage capacitors can hold a lethal charge even after power is removed.

fixSteps.title: Clear Debris
fixSteps.instruction: Pull disconnect and inspect/clean fan blade area.

fixSteps.title: Replace Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install matching motor with same RPM and HP.

whenToCallPro: Motor replacement best done by a pro.

faq.q: Can I run AC without outdoor fan?
faq.a: No - it will rapidly overheat the compressor and trip high pressure.

title: EEPROM Memory Fault
shortDescription: Control board cannot read configuration memory.
fullDescription: Goodman E9 indicates the control board's EEPROM (where calibration and configuration are stored) cannot be read or has been corrupted.
safetyWarning: Disconnect power at the breaker before opening control panels. High-voltage capacitors can hold a lethal charge even after power is removed.

fixSteps.title: Pro Replace Board
fixSteps.instruction: Board needs replacement and reconfiguration by a Goodman dealer.

whenToCallPro: Always pro - boards must be configured to system.

faq.a: No - new boards need dipswitches and configuration set to match the system.

title: Liquid Line Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Liquid line temperature sensor out of range.
fullDescription: Goodman E10 indicates the liquid line thermistor is reading invalid values. The sensor is used for charge verification on inverter systems.
safetyWarning: Refrigerant work requires EPA Section 608 certification. Improper handling can cause frostbite, asphyxiation, or environmental harm.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Mount
fixSteps.instruction: Verify thermistor is clamped tight to liquid line under insulation.

fixSteps.title: Replace Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new thermistor with thermal paste.

whenToCallPro: Pro if you are not comfortable working near the refrigerant lines.

faq.q: Why does charge depend on this?
faq.a: Liquid line temperature plus pressure tells the controller subcooling, which sets charge accuracy.

title: Pressure Switch Stuck Open
shortDescription: Low pressure switch did not close.
fullDescription: Pressure switch stuck open during call for cool. Inspect refrigerant charge and switch wiring.

fixSteps.title: Verify wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check pressure switch and sensor wiring.

whenToCallPro: Sealed system or compressor diagnostics require a licensed HVAC technician.

faq.a: Low pressure switch did not close.

title: Pressure Switch Stuck Closed
shortDescription: High pressure switch did not open at startup.
fullDescription: Switch stuck closed condition detected. Replace switch.

fixSteps.title: Verify wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check pressure switch and sensor wiring.

whenToCallPro: Sealed system or compressor diagnostics require a licensed HVAC technician.

faq.a: High pressure switch did not open at startup.

fullDescription: Compressor drew current above limits. Possible mechanical or electrical fault.

title: Reversing Valve Fault
fullDescription: Reversing valve solenoid coil failed continuity test. Replace solenoid.

fixSteps.title: Verify wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Check pressure switch and sensor wiring.

title: Outdoor Coil Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E21 on Goodman ComfortBridge AC indicates the outdoor coil temperature sensor is reading out of range.
whenToCallPro: If sensor and wiring are OK, replace control board.

faq.a: Clipped to the outdoor coil tubing.

title: Discharge Line Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E22 indicates the compressor discharge line sensor is malfunctioning.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Trace from discharge line to outdoor board.

fixSteps.title: Replace
fixSteps.instruction: Clip new sensor to discharge line.

whenToCallPro: If E22 persists, suspect outdoor control board.

faq.a: Eventually — discharge protection will trip without valid sensor.

title: Liquid Line Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E23 is set when the liquid line thermistor reads out of range.
whenToCallPro: If sensor checks out, board may be faulty.

faq.q: What does liquid line sensor do?
faq.a: Helps the board calculate subcool for charging diagnostics.

title: Outdoor Ambient Sensor Fault
fullDescription: E24 indicates the outdoor air temperature sensor is open or shorted.
symptoms: Logic that depends on outdoor temp disabled

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Find on outdoor unit, near the coil.

whenToCallPro: If sensor is fine, control board may need replacement.

faq.a: Yes, but advanced features may be disabled.

title: Outdoor Fan Motor Fault
shortDescription: Condenser fan not running at commanded speed.
fullDescription: E25 indicates the outdoor fan motor failed to reach the commanded RPM.

fixSteps.title: Visual Check
fixSteps.instruction: Power off; spin blade by hand.

whenToCallPro: If electrical components test fine but error persists, suspect outdoor board.
safetyWarning: Capacitors retain lethal charge.

title: Compressor Overcurrent
fullDescription: E26 is set when the outdoor board sees compressor amps above the threshold for its model.

fixSteps.title: Pro Diagnosis
fixSteps.instruction: Compressor amp draw vs LRA spec.

faq.a: Sometimes — adds torque on startup, can mask weak compressor.

title: Compressor Lockout
fullDescription: E27 is a 24-hour lockout after repeated compressor faults. Manual reset required.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cut breaker 5 minutes for diagnostic reset.

fixSteps.title: Find Root Cause
fixSteps.instruction: Don't simply reset — diagnose with a tech.

title: Indoor Communications Lost
shortDescription: ComfortBridge lost serial link to indoor unit.
fullDescription: E28 means the outdoor controller cannot communicate with the indoor air handler/furnace via ComfortBridge.

fixSteps.title: Tighten Wires
fixSteps.instruction: Check ComfortBridge terminals at indoor and outdoor.

fixSteps.title: Replace Cable
fixSteps.instruction: Pull new thermostat cable if damaged.

faq.a: Yes in legacy mode, but ComfortBridge features disabled.

title: Power Line Noise
fullDescription: E29 is reported when ComfortBridge sees excessive bus errors due to electrical noise.

causes.cause: Nearby variable-frequency drive or large motor

fixSteps.title: Check Grounds
fixSteps.instruction: Verify equipment ground at both indoor and outdoor.

fixSteps.title: Re-route Cable
fixSteps.instruction: Move comm cable away from line voltage.

fixSteps.title: Add Ferrite Cores
fixSteps.instruction: Snap ferrite chokes on the comm cable ends.

whenToCallPro: Persistent noise issues need a service tech with scope.

title: Outdoor Board Hardware Fault
fullDescription: E30 fires when the outdoor board's startup self-test failed. Replacement is the standard remedy.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Cut breaker 5 minutes; sometimes clears EEPROM glitch.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Board
fixSteps.instruction: Look for burn marks, swollen capacitors.

whenToCallPro: Always — outdoor board work involves line voltage.

faq.a: Yes — HVAC surge protection extends control life.

safetyWarning: Line voltage is present at the outdoor board even with thermostat off.
